The '''48th Academy Awards''' were presented Monday, March 29, 1976, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Los Angeles]], California. The ceremonies were presided over by [[Walter Matthau]], [[Robert Shaw (actor)|Robert Shaw]], [[George Segal]], [[Goldie Hawn]], and [[Gene Kelly]].

[[Miloš Forman]]'s ''[[One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (film)|One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest]]'' made a "[[List of Big Five Academy Award winners and nominees|clean sweep]]" of the five major categories: [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]], [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] and [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Screenplay (Adapted)]]. It was the second of three films to date to do so, following ''[[It Happened One Night]]'' in [[7th Academy Awards|1934]] and preceding ''[[The Silence of the Lambs (film)|The Silence of the Lambs]]'' in [[64th Academy Awards|1991]].

20-year-old French actress [[Isabelle Adjani]] received her first nomination for Best Actress this year, becoming the youngest nominee that category, breaking the record set by 22-year-old [[Elizabeth Hartman]] in [[38th Academy Awards|1965]]. Her record would be surpassed by 13-year-old [[Keisha Castle-Hughes]] in 2004, and again in 2013 by nine-year old [[Quvenzhané Wallis]], the current record. Adjani also co-presented the award for [[Academy Award for Best Film Editing|Best Film Editing]].

At 80, [[George Burns]] became the [[List of oldest and youngest Academy Award winners and nominees|oldest]] acting winner, as well as the last person born in the nineteenth century to receive an acting award. His record stood until [[Jessica Tandy]] won Best Actress in [[62nd Academy Awards|1989]]; Burns was later succeeded as the oldest [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] winner by [[Christopher Plummer]], who won in 2012 for ''[[Beginners]]'' at the age of 82.

''[[Jaws (film)|Jaws]]'' won all its nominations except Best Picture, the last film to do so until ''[[Traffic (2000 film)|Traffic]]''. As of the [[94th Academy Awards]], ''[[Amarcord]]'', nominated for Best Director, is the last film to be nominated for Academy Awards in separate years (having won the award for [[Academy Award for Best Foreign Film|Best Foreign Language Film]] the [[47th Academy Awards|year before]]).

This ceremony marked the return of Oscar telecasts to [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], which carried the event from [[33rd Academy Awards|1961]] until [[NBC]] held the rights for a 5-year period beginning in [[43rd Academy Awards|1971]]. (ABC has maintained Oscar TV rights to this day.) [[NBC Sports|NBC's]] coverage of the [[1976 NCAA Division I basketball championship game|NCAA Division I basketball championship]] aired the same night as the ceremony, and while Adjani unsealed the envelope for Best Film Editing, co-presenter [[Elliott Gould]] jokingly announced the winner as "[[1975–76 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]], 86-68" (the title game's outcome in [[Spectrum (arena)|Philadelphia]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hughes |first=James |date=2013-11-19 |title=The Sporting Life of Elliott Gould |url=https://grantland.com/features/the-life-career-actor-elliott-gould/ |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=Grantland |language=en-US}}</ref>
